pluss::subsp::stats::ts::ArimaOptions¶

Options of ts::Arima::fit_mle: the orders of the model, starting values and search settings.

ArimaOptions names the regular orders (ar_order, diff_order, ma_order), the seasonal orders and period, and how the likelihood is maximised.

Field

Type

Default

Meaning

std::int64_t

1

Number of autoregressive coefficients p.

diff_order

std::int64_t

0

Number of regular differences d taken before fitting.

ma_order

std::int64_t

0

Number of moving-average coefficients q.

seasonal_ar_order

std::int64_t

0

Number of seasonal autoregressive coefficients P (at multiples of the period).

seasonal_diff_order

std::int64_t

Number of seasonal differences D.

seasonal_ma_order

0

Number of seasonal moving-average coefficients Q.

seasonal_period

std::int64_t

0

The season length s; it must exceed 1 when any seasonal order is used.

demean

bool

true

Subtract the sample mean first; a further free constant (intercept) is estimated as well.

intercept0

double

0

Starting value of the intercept.

ar0, ma0, sar0, sma0

std::vector<double>

empty

Starting values of the four coefficient groups; empty means the zero polynomial, which is valid.

beta0

std::vector<double>

empty

Starting values of the regression coefficients when exogenous regressors are used.

variance_floor

double

1e-12

Smallest innovation variance the search accepts.

stationarity_margin

double

1e-6

The partial autocorrelations are kept inside ±(1 − margin).

finite_diff_eps

double

1e-5

Step of the numerical derivatives used by score and observed_inf.

max_iterations, max_evaluations

std::int64_t

800, 6000

Limits of the Nelder–Mead search.

simplex_delta

double

0.05

Relative size of the initial simplex.

exact_likelihood

bool

true

true: the exact Gaussian likelihood (Kalman filter, stationary start). false: the conditional likelihood that skips the first max(p, q) observations. Models with exogenous regressors always use the conditional likelihood.

Guidance¶

Choose the orders from the autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions and confirm by comparing log-likelihoods and information criteria of neighbouring models. Starting values rarely matter: the search is over a parametrisation in which every candidate is valid, and the zero start is well inside it.
